Our Research Contact Us
Research Areas

Core Research Areas

Our laboratory pursues innovative drug candidates across ten interconnected research areas — spanning oncology target modulation (transcription factors, ubiquitination pathways, protein kinases including Hippo pathway), organosulfur and nucleoside chemistry, next-generation bioconjugation (ADC), peptide-based scaffolds, green synthesis technologies (microfluidics, mechanochemistry), and boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT).

01

Direct Modulation of Oncogenic Transcription Factors

＋

Direct inhibition of oncogenic transcription factors using small molecules. Targeting protein–DNA interactions (PDI) and protein–protein interactions (PPI) to suppress c-Myc, YAP-TEAD, and related targets.

Oncology / Transcription Factor
02

Regulation of Ubiquitination Pathways

＋

Development of small-molecule inhibitors targeting ubiquitin-like activating enzymes E1 (UAE, NAE, SAE). Selective modulation of the ubiquitin–proteasome system for anticancer applications.

UBL E1 / Ubiquitination
03

Protein Kinase Inhibitors

＋

Design and optimization of small-molecule inhibitors targeting aberrantly activated protein kinases. Employing selective covalent inhibition strategies and systematic SAR studies. Current focus includes Hippo pathway-related kinases (LATS1/2, MST1/2) as emerging targets in regenerative medicine and oncology.

Kinase Inhibitor / Drug Design
04

Organosulfur Chemistry-Based Drug Discovery

＋

Synthesis and medicinal chemistry application of organosulfur(IV) compounds including sulfoximines, sulfilimines, and N-cyano sulfoximines. Covering COX inhibition, anticancer activity, and amide bond bioisostere studies.

Organosulfur / Heterocycle
05

Nucleoside Analogues

＋

Development of small molecules based on nucleoside-mimicking structures. Exploring novel anticancer mechanisms through post-translational modification (PTM) regulation.

Nucleoside / Antiviral
06

Antibody–Drug Conjugate (ADC) Chemistry

＋

Development of bioorthogonal ADC conjugation strategies based on N-cyano sulfoximine–thiazole ligation. Achieving uniform DAR and high stability on trastuzumab and related antibodies.

ADC / Bioconjugation
07

Peptide-Based Drug Discovery

＋

Drug discovery inspired by natural cyclic peptides such as lasso peptides. Exploring target selectivity and protease resistance enabled by unique three-dimensional scaffolds.

Peptide / Natural Products
08

Microfluidics Process Development

＋

Optimization of microfluidic synthesis processes for ADC and nanoparticle formulations. Significantly reducing reaction time and improving conjugation uniformity compared to batch processes.

Process Chemistry / Microfluidics
09

Mechanochemistry

＋

Green organic synthesis using mechanical energy without solvents. Exploring solid-state reactions via ball milling to replace solution-phase processes and discover novel reactivity.

Mechanochemistry / Green Chemistry
10

Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT)

＋

Design and synthesis of boron-containing compounds for Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT). Developing tumor-selective boron delivery agents with enhanced metabolic stability and water solubility, leveraging noncanonical amino acid scaffolds and bioorthogonal chemistry for precise cancer treatment.

BNCT / Boron Chemistry

Research 2026.04

🏅 Journal Cover Selected — RSC Mechanochemistry

Our paper "Mechanoredox Radical Annulation for the Solvent-Free Synthesis of 2-Substituted Benzothiophenes" has been selected as the journal cover of RSC Mechanochemistry. Congratulations to all co-authors!

Award 2026.04

🏆 Best Poster Award — KCS 137th General Meeting

Congratulations to Eun-Sil Kim (Ph.D. candidate, UST) on receiving the Best Poster Award at the 137th General Meeting of the Korean Chemical Society (April 15–17, 2026, ICC Jeju). Excellent work!

KCS 137th General Meeting & Exhibition

Lab members attended the 137th General Meeting of the Korean Chemical Society, April 15–17, 2026, ICC Jeju.

Academic 2026.04

Poster Presentations at KCS 137th General Meeting

EunSol Jo presented "Development of Cyclic Boron-Containing Amino Acids as an Antibody–Boron Conjugate Platform for Precision BNCT" and Ji Ho Song presented "Mechanoredox Radical Annulation under Solvent-Free Conditions for the Synthesis of 2-Substituted Benzothiophenes" as poster presentations at the 137th General Meeting of the Korean Chemical Society (April 15–17, 2026, ICC Jeju).
